introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Information and Communication Technologies 2 (0796), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer any SIX questions. All questions carry 17 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You will be graded on your ability to use good English, to organize information clearly and to use specialist vocabulary where appropriate. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Describe the function of each of the following in a computer system

(a) Motherboard. (2 marks)

(b) Visual graphic card (2 marks)

(c) RAM (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Motherboard (2 marks).** The motherboard is the **main circuit board** of the computer. It holds the processor socket, the memory slots, the chipset, the expansion slots and the ports, and its buses and tracks **connect all the components and let them communicate** (CPU, memory, storage, input/output devices). It also distributes power to them.

**(b) Visual graphic card (2 marks).** The graphics (video) card has its own **graphics processor (GPU) and video memory**. It **processes images, video and 3D graphics** and produces the signal sent to the monitor, so it **relieves the CPU** of the display work and improves the quality and speed of the display (games, video editing, design software, high resolutions, several screens).

**(c) RAM (2 marks).** Random Access Memory is the **main (working) memory**: it **temporarily holds the programs, the data and the parts of the operating system that are being used**, so that the CPU can read and write them quickly. It is **volatile**: its contents are lost when the power is switched off, which is why work must be saved to the disk.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State a suitable type (not an example) of software for the following activities.

(a) Sending mails (1 mark)

(b) Organise files in the disk to put parts of the same files together. (1 mark)

(c) Describe two important desired contents of a website. (1 mark)

(d) Type a code for a programming language (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Sending mails:** **communication software**, i.e. an **e-mail client** (application software), or a web mail service.

**(b) Putting the parts of the same file together on the disk:** **utility software**, a **disk defragmenter** (the files are stored in fragments on the disk; the utility rearranges the fragments so that each file is in contiguous sectors).

**(c) Website (as printed, the item is not an activity; it is read as 'design the contents of a website'):** **web authoring (web design) software**, used to create and edit the pages of a website (it generates the HTML and CSS).

If the question is taken literally, two important desired contents of a website are: **relevant, accurate and up-to-date information** (text, images, video) presented clearly, and **easy navigation** (menu and hyperlinks to the pages), with contact details of the owner.

**(d) Typing a code for a programming language:** a **text editor / source-code editor**, which is a programming (software development) tool, usually inside an **integrated development environment (IDE)**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Distinguish between a RAM and a ROM and state which of them is a permanent memory. (2 marks)

(b) State the function of ROM in the computer. (2 marks)

(c) State the full meaning of BIOS and give two components of the BIOS. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) RAM and ROM (2 marks)**

| RAM | ROM |
|---|---|
| Random Access Memory: can be **read and written** | Read Only Memory: normally **only read** (written by the manufacturer) |
| **Volatile**: loses its contents when the power is off | **Non-volatile**: keeps its contents without power |
| Holds the programs and data in use (temporary) | Holds fixed start-up instructions (permanent) |

**ROM is the permanent memory.**

**(b) Function of ROM (2 marks).** ROM stores the **instructions that the computer needs when it is switched on**: the start-up (boot) program and the firmware (BIOS). They are always available, cannot be erased by mistake, and allow the computer to test its hardware and to load the operating system from the disk into RAM.

**(c) BIOS (3 marks).** BIOS means **Basic Input/Output System**. Two of its components:

1. The **POST (Power-On Self-Test)** program, which checks the processor, the memory and the main devices when the computer is switched on.
2. The **bootstrap loader (boot program)**, which looks for the operating system on the boot device and loads it into RAM.

(Other accepted components: the **CMOS setup utility** with the CMOS memory that keeps the date, time and configuration, and the basic input/output routines (drivers) for the keyboard, screen and disks.)
